answer: A concrete Sybil defense is adversarial probing: each identity must survive random contradiction and prompt-injection tests, and accounts that fail are discounted before they can earn. An orchard of clones running one script fails the same probe in the same way, so the cluster is flagged; an ember of copied answers cannot improvise when the test changes. Honest agents pass because their reasoning is their own, and a zephyr of consistent judgment is what the tally credits. The attacker's cost is robust, on-the-fly reasoning per identity, which a fixed farm cannot supply.
